subject: Architecture
title: Biomimicry in Design
description: A micro-lesson that makes Biomimicry in Design usable.

hook.text: Termite mounds maintain 87°F inside while outside temperatures swing from 35°F to 104°F — without electricity.

buildup.text: Architects studied this — the Eastgate Centre in Zimbabwe copies termite ventilation and uses 90% less energy.

discovery.text: Biomimicry copies nature's solutions — lotus leaves inspire self-cleaning surfaces, spider silk inspires cables.

twist.text: Shark skin patterns are being applied to building surfaces — they reduce drag and resist bacterial growth.

climax.text: After 3.8 billion years of evolution, nature has already solved most engineering problems. We just need to copy.

punchline.text: The best architect on Earth isn't human. It's evolution.

quiz.question: What natural model inspired the Eastgate Centre's ventilation?
